svg.title: One Inverse to Rule the Video Aisles
svg.desc: Four-panel comic in a video shop. Panel 1, EASE with 4 videos: the recommender keeps one table that scores every video against every video (16 cells, a dark cell means two videos are often liked together), solves it in one step, and often beats deep nets. Panel 2, EASE with 40 videos: the boss announces 10 times more videos, the table grows to 1,600 cells and the work to 1,000 times, so the recommender is still calculating. Panel 3, ELSA with 4 videos: each video gets just 3 aisle scores (12 cells), aisles the system found from viewing alone with no tags; similar scores mean similar videos. Panel 4, ELSA with 40 videos: the same news adds only rows, 120 cells and 10 times the work, so the recommender is done and offers coffee. EASE fills an n by n table, work grows with n cubed; ELSA fills an n by d table, work grows with n times d squared.
svg.text: One Inverse to Rule the Video Aisles

text.tspan: one table, solved in one step.

svg.text: EASE fills an n × n table: 10× the videos, 1,000× the work (n³).
ELSA fills an n × d table (d aisles): 10× the videos, 10× the work (n·d²).
